chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Strayhorn and Ellington as alter egos and credit for Strayhorn's work
summary: Barnet thinks Strayhorn's delicacy needed Duke's soloists and that he did not care about credit, while Barney Bigard was salty about it.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: couldn't have found anybody to interpret what he was doing -- well, you get back to the old thing, the alter ego, the association there. You couldn't tell where one left off and the other started, and without each other -- well, let's put it this way. I doubt very much if we'd have heard much about Billy if he hadn't gotten associated with Duke, because he was too subtle in a very rough world of music. Of course I think if I could have found him I might have been able to do something, but on the other hand where would he have gotten the soloists? I never had the soloists that Duke had. Well, you keep bouncing back and forth. I mean if one, what would the other had done, and the other and the other and the other. It comes back that I think that was truly an alter ego situation.

Yeah. They had an amazing kind of a communication, and were, as you say, great complements, because Duke needed the attention and Billy didn't care about it, which was fine, because if they had both wanted recognition there would have been a clash.
Oh, it would have been a catastrophe.

They'd have been in court, arguing about who wrote this eight bars and that eight bars. Because I know of a lot of cases where they actually did, one would start an arrangement and the other would finish it.

It's a question of where -- who owns it the, you know? But Billy did write a lot of things that were either erroneously credited to Duke or -- I won't go so far as to say deliberately, but I mean Duke Ellington was so big that anything that came out of there automatically -- even if Juan Tizol did it -- it was credited to Duke, because it came out of there. He was such an awe inspiring figure.
Uh-huh. But the difference with Billy was that Billy didn't care.
So long as the music got written and --
Barney was a little salty about it.
Yes, yes, Barney was, and still is a little bit, although he's philosophical. He -- I don't think he's mad at anybody, but he said there was 20 years of royalties he could have used.
